brief: FOMC's Oct 27-28 minutes showed almost all participants favoring further rate hikes to return inflation to 2%, and Fed officials Waller, Goolsbee and Cook reinforced the hawkish message that week, with Waller pushing for a 50bp December hike. The S&P 500 closed 10.8% below its Oct 28 level and the Nasdaq 100 fell 16% over the same stretch. Investor Sparks (interviewed by One River's Peters) argues AI is the first existential-risk technology humanity cannot contain, because unlike nuclear weapons it requires no scarce input and recursive self-improvement would make it both necessary and impossible to understand or turn off. He expects 1-3 years of disruption as old systems meet it. From there he argues markets are circularly levered to the AI trade, earnings are 30% above trend, and stocks are 40-50% overvalued even ignoring Fed tightening, so the market should already be down 40-50% before an eventual debate over shutting AI off. He recommends 3-5 year Treasuries. The piece also notes Nvidia's post-earnings pop reversed into a 23% weekly loss, and recalls February 2018's 96% one-afternoon inverse-VIX wipeout as a precedent for crowd-driven flushes.
